title: Memory Chip Wobble: Kioxia Sinks, SK Hynix Sees Shortage Through 2030
summary: Gotrade News - Kioxia shares fell 11% in early Tokyo trading on Monday, according to TECHi , after the flash memory maker guided December-quarter
body_markdown:
Monday's drop also followed a heavy Friday for US chip stocks. As reported by Bloomingbit, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 7.2% on October 30 after major tech earnings missed expectations, with[Intel posting its biggest drop in more than four decades](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/intel-plunges-21-on-weak-pc-guidance-chip-stocks-sell-off/) . Shoji Hirakawa, chief global strategist at Tokai Tokyo Intelligence Lab, said Kioxia's disappointing outlook "could heighten concerns about profitability across Japan's technology sector," per Bloomingbit.


## SK Hynix (SKHY): Demand Seen Above Supply Through 2030


SK Hynix struck a different tone with its results last week. According to[SK hynix's third-quarter release](https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/sk-hynix-announces-3q26-financial-results-20261028) , revenue reached 104.6155 trillion won and operating profit 83.3338 trillion won, an 80% operating margin. The company said it "expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030," and that long-term agreements with 14 major customers cover more than 50% of its total production capacity for 2027 and 2028.


As reported by[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/sk-hynix-posts-record-revenue-and-profit-sees-memory-shortage-into-2030-113038822.html) , operating profit rose 632% from a year earlier, US-listed SK Hynix shares rose more than 9% on Wednesday, October 28, and[Micron (MU)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mu/) rose 4% the same day. RBC Capital Markets analyst Srini Pajjuri wrote: "Robust AI demand, coupled with a shift toward memory-intensive agentic AI, continues to outpace supply."


The Seoul shares eased on Monday. Per[TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/more/262263133-japan-korea-stocks-skhy-kospi-nikkei-samsung-kioxia-ai-softbank-fomc-usa-tradingkey) , SK Hynix fell 1.4% to 1,399,000 won in early trading on November 2, Samsung Electronics dropped 3% to 218,500 won, and the KOSPI slipped 1.10% to 5,667.49 as semiconductors weighed on the index.


## Sandisk (SNDK): Shares Fell 13.5% in Friday's Chip Selloff


NAND peer[Sandisk (SNDK)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/sndk/) had already slid before Kioxia's Tokyo session. According to Yahoo Finance, Sandisk closed at $1,150.89 on October 30, down 13.47% from the previous session, on a day TECHi noted the broader US market was also weak.


Sandisk's own guidance calls for fiscal second-quarter revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion, as reported by TECHi, after fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 23% from the prior quarter to $11.031 billion and data-center revenue rose 61% to $4.802 billion. TECHi also noted that an eight-for-one stock split takes effect later in November, and wrote of Kioxia: "Flat guidance after exceptional growth is not the same as collapsing demand."
